title: Responder capability map and incident evidence SOP
author: Samira Patel
content:
Summary:
This page defines a compact responder capability map and the standard operating procedure (SOP) for collecting incident evidence at Redwood Inference. The goal is to ensure first responders can: (1) quickly identify the likely failure domain, (2) collect forensically useful evidence without worsening system state, and (3) hand off to follow-up owners with reproducible context and artifacts.

Purpose and scope:
- Purpose: Reduce time-to-diagnosis by standardizing who does what in the first 20 minutes of an incident and what evidence to capture.
- Scope: Applies to LLM-serving incidents across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments that impact latency, throughput, correctness (model quality regressions), or availability. Does NOT replace service-specific runbooks but complements them with responder capability mapping and evidence collection guidance.

Quick reference (one-line):
- Priority A (P0/P1 service outage or major degradation): follow the "P0 responder path" in Section "P0 response checklist" and capture evidence set A.
- Priority B (partial or non-customer visible anomaly): follow "P1/P2 triage" and capture evidence set B.

Responder capability map (who does what):
- Primary responder (pager): initial triage, short-term mitigation, status updates. Skills: kubectl, logs->structured trace search, basic runtime metrics. Owned by on-call service engineer. Escalation: SRE lead at +10m if no stabilization steps succeed.
- Platform SRE: capacity routing, autoscaler, cluster-level alerts, and infra-level mitigations (cordon/drain, node reboot).
- Serving-runtime engineer: kernel selection, batching/quantization issues, KV cache invalidation.
- Model owner (applied-ml): quality regressions, hallucinations, evals.
- Customer operations (customer-success): customer-facing comms for enterprise-impacting incidents.

Responsibility matrix (short table):
- Detection: Alerting system (PagerDuty + internal bridge)
- First response: Primary responder
- Containment: Primary responder + Platform SRE
- Mitigation: Serving-runtime or Platform SRE depending on domain
- Root cause & fix: Serving-runtime / Applied-ML / Infra teams

Evidence collection SOP (principles):
1) Minimum impact: prefer read-only commands and aggregated exports. Avoid restarts/rollbacks until initial evidence snapshot is taken unless customer-impacting severity mandates immediate mitigation.
2) Time-bound: target 0–10 minute snapshot, 10–30 minute deep snapshot, and 30–90 minute extended evidence set.
3) Reproducibility: tag exports with epoch timestamps and correlate with PagerDuty incident ID and bridge link.

Evidence sets (concrete lists):
- Evidence set A (P0/P1 - urgent, must capture within first 10 minutes):
  - Incident ID, service name, region, and user-visible symptom description.
  - p95/p99 latency and error-rate graphs (link to dashboard + 1 PNG export).
  - Top 50 logs from affected service (structured JSON lines) covering -5m..+5m relative to the incident trigger. Command: 
    kubectl logs -l app=redwood-serving -n production --since=10m --tail=500 --timestamps > logs_0-10m.json
  - Recent deployment/version metadata: git SHA, model version tag, rollout ID.
  - Player/process status (node-level): free memory, GPU utilization, OOM events. Commands: nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu,memory.used --format=csv; dmesg | tail -n 200
  - Runtime KV cache stats and top cache keys (if KV cache enabled). API example: curl -s http://runtime-admin.local/kvcache/stats > kvcache_stats.json
  - Active inflight request sampling (top 20 traces).
  - PagerDuty timeline + initial on-call notes (copy into incident log).

- Evidence set B (P2/P3 - non-urgent, deeper analysis 10–60m):
  - Full traces for 100 sampled requests (links/exports).
  - Batching histograms and sequence length distribution for last 60m.
  - Autoscaler decisions and recent scaling events with timestamps.
  - Disk I/O and network queues for node pools.
  - Model performance metrics (per-prompt token generation time) and any recent model promotions in last 24h.

Standard commands and ephemeral scripts (copy/paste):
- Snapshot metrics (Prometheus): curl -s "https://prometheus.internal/api/v1/query?query=up" > prom_up.json
- Export traces (observability): curl -s "https://obs.internal/api/trace/export?incident_id=INC1234&limit=100" > traces_sample.json
- Kubernetes snapshot: kubectl get pods -n production -o wide --all-namespaces > pods_snapshot.txt
- Model endpoint list: redwoodctl endpoints list --region us-west1 --json > endpoints.json

P0 response checklist (first 20 minutes):
1) Ack incident in PagerDuty and open bridge. Record incident ID and bridge URL.
2) Take evidence set A using commands above. Attach artifacts to incident ticket.
3) Identify if incident is infra-level (node/GPU), runtime-level, model-level, or network. Use triage decision ladder: resumeable errors > resource exhaustion > model regressions > external dependency failure.
4) If containment is possible without restart (traffic cut, fallback route), apply containment and continue gathering evidence. Document steps taken.
5) If immediate restart/rollback is required to restore service, document the exact commands, time, and reason; still attach evidence pre-change if possible.

Escalation matrix (phone + PD + slack):
- After 10 minutes unresolved at P0: escalate to SRE lead (pager + call).
- After 30 minutes unresolved: paging engineering manager and product on-call.
- Customer-grade incidents: notify customer-ops within first 15 minutes.

On-call rotation and handoff policy (compact):
- Rotation length: 7 days for service engineers; 14 days for platform SRE.
- Handover window: 30 minute overlap recommended. Handoff checklist: open incidents, mitigations applied, pending actions, and evidence artifacts location.
- Shadowing: new on-call participants must shadow one full incident-response cycle and run 2 game-day exercises in their first rotation.

Game day blueprint (short):
- Frequency: quarterly cross-team game days; targeted subsystems monthly (runtime, autoscaler, KV cache).
- Goals: exercise evidence collection end-to-end, measure time to attach artifacts to ticket, and practice customer comms.
- Metrics to capture: time-to-first-evidence, time-to-first-stable-state, percentage of incidents with complete evidence set A attached within 20 minutes.

Postmortem and RCA template (what must be present):
- Title, incident ID, timeline (UTC), severity, impacted customers and regions.
- Summary: 3-sentence incident summary.
- Detection: how alert triggered and first notification time.
- Containment & mitigation: who did what and when (timestamps).
- Root cause hypothesis and evidence linking (explicitly cite artifacts saved during incident).
- Corrective actions: short-term, medium-term, long-term owners and due dates.
- Severity classification and customer remediation/credits (if any).

Customer status message templates (concise, two flavors):
- Initial short (public status page):
  "We are investigating increased latency for text-generation requests in US-West. Our engineers have identified a partial capacity issue and are actively mitigating. No action required from customers; updates at 15-minute cadence"
- Enterprise direct (private):
  "[Customer], we detected elevated error rates on model X in your us-west tenant. The primary cause appears to be a node-level memory pressure event impacting KV cache efficiency. We have applied capacity routing to reduce customer impact and will share a detailed timeline within 2 hours. Incident ID: INC-2025-12345."

Evidence retention and ticketing (must-dos):
- Attach all evidence artifacts to the incident ticket in the internal bridge and the postmortem doc.
- Evidence filenames should include incident ID, timestamp, and artifact type: e.g., INC-2025-12345_logs_20250201T1312.json
- Store large exports (traces >50MB) in S3 under s3://redwood-incidents/INC-2025-12345/ and reference the signed URL in the ticket.

Appendix A — Minimal forensic checklist (0–10 min):
- copy: incident ID, bridge link, p95/p99 screenshot, top 500 log lines, pods_snapshot.txt, nvidia-smi output, kvcache_stats.json, endpoints.json

Appendix B — Helpful links and runbooks:
- Observability runbook: https://confluence.internal/observability/runbook
- Runtime emergency rollback: https://confluence.internal/eng-serving-runtime/release-rollbacks
- PagerDuty playbook: https://confluence.internal/oncall-and-incident-response/pagerduty-usage

Ownership and maintenance:

- Review cadence: annually or after any P0 incident.
